items.title: Purchase Order
items.context: Material Management › Procure-to-Pay (PO Flow) › Purchase Order

cards.title: When does a buyer raise a purchase order, and which earlier documents can it be converted from?
cards.body:
A buyer raises a **purchase order** when goods or services must be ordered from a vendor.
It can convert an approved **indent**, LOI, quotation or agreement, or be a **drop-shipment** against a sales order or GRC.

cards.title: Where does the purchase order sit in Procure-to-Pay, between comparing quotations and receiving goods?
cards.body:
The **purchase order** comes after quotations are compared and before the goods arrive.
The buyer compares vendor quotations, places the order, the gate records the inward vehicle, and stores record the **goods receipt**.

cards.title: What is the validity date on a purchase order, and what is the earliest date it can carry?
cards.body:
The **validity date** is a required date on every order and cannot be earlier than the **order date**.
Under a company rule it must also equal the latest **schedule date**, as a warning or a block.
source_refs: Purchase Order: Validity Equals Last Schedule Rule [4:478dbad0-cd96-4aa4-bac7-6d61036ab7b0:80451] (rule:purchase-order-validity-equals-last-schedule-rule)
Mandatory fields and valid selections on documents [4:478dbad0-cd96-4aa4-bac7-6d61036ab7b0:79742] (rule:mandatory-document-fields)

cards.title: What is an authorization group on a purchase order, and how does the order's value decide which one applies?
cards.body:
An **authorization group** is the set of approvers for an order, picked by the order's **net amount**.
Each group covers an amount range, and the group is chosen again whenever the net amount changes.
source_refs: Purchase Order: Group by Net Amount [4:478dbad0-cd96-4aa4-bac7-6d61036ab7b0:80422] (rule:purchase-order-group-by-net-amount)

cards.title: What does repeating a previous purchase order copy, and what starts fresh on the new order?
cards.body:
**Repeat previous order** copies a chosen earlier order into a brand-new order only.
The date, number and prefix are reset, and the copy starts in **Initial** status.
source_refs: Bulk entry follows the listed format and checks [4:478dbad0-cd96-4aa4-bac7-6d61036ab7b0:78936] (rule:fast-entry-excel-import)

cards.title: When does the system build the delivery schedule for a purchase order automatically?
cards.body:
For a **Direct** order, the system generates the **delivery schedule** for the lines when the **auto schedule** setting is on.
A Direct order is one placed without a source document such as an indent.

cards.title: What is a consignee location on a purchase order, and how many must the buyer give?
cards.body:
Every purchase order needs at least one valid **consignee location**.
When a line is split across consignees, each consignee needs its own **item detail**.

cards.title: Which payment and billing parties must the buyer name on every purchase order before it saves?
cards.body:
Every order names a **Pay To** party and location, a **Billed To** party and location, and a **payment mode**.
Payment terms are also checked, except on orders against a DO.

cards.title: Can the buyer give both a freight amount and a freight order on the same purchase order leg?
cards.body:
No: a leg or the header carries either a **freight amount** or a **freight order**, never both.
A freight amount is saved only when it is above zero.
source_refs: Purchase Order: Freight Amount or Freight Order [4:478dbad0-cd96-4aa4-bac7-6d61036ab7b0:80421] (rule:purchase-order-freight-amount-or-freight-order)

cards.title: Where do the terms and conditions and payment terms on a new purchase order come from?
cards.body:
The **terms and conditions** and **payment terms** of an order are filled in from the **vendor location**.
So choosing the vendor location also brings in that location's terms.

cards.title: What must each item be linked to before the buyer can order it on a purchase that is not under GST?
cards.body:
On a **non-GST purchase**, each item must be linked to a **chapter heading**.
An item with no chapter heading link is refused, and the refusal names the item.

cards.title: Can a purchase order line carry a zero rate or a zero quantity, and what does the buyer enter?
cards.body:
The **rate** must be entered but may be zero; the **quantity** must be above zero.
A line with no rate, or with zero quantity, stops the save.

cards.title: Why must lines of the same item on one purchase order share the same order unit and rate?
cards.body:
Lines of the same item on one order must use the same **order unit** and the same **rate**.
A different unit or rate on a second line of that item is refused.
For example, two lines of one item at 120 and 125 per unit cannot be saved together.

cards.title: Can the buyer add the same item twice to one purchase order with the same make and technical grade?
cards.body:
No: the same item with the same **make** and **technical grade** cannot repeat on one order.
Every order also needs at least one item line.
source_refs: Names, codes and aliases must be unique [4:478dbad0-cd96-4aa4-bac7-6d61036ab7b0:82501] (rule:unique-master-names)

cards.title: Why is a capital item refused on a General purchase order, and what else cannot be mixed?
cards.body:
A **capital item** cannot be ordered on a **General** order.
Capital and non-capital items cannot share one order, and items of different item types cannot be mixed.

cards.title: How does the system decide whether a purchase order came from a sales order, an indent or no source?
cards.body:
The **order origin** comes from the source lines the buyer selects.
It is a sales order, a GRC task or an **indent**, depending on those lines, and **Direct** when none applies.

cards.title: What happens to the purchase type, category and reference type when the buyer changes the document type?
cards.body:
Changing the **document type** resets the **purchase type**, purchase category and reference document type.
The buyer chooses the document type first, then fills those fields again.

cards.title: Who can still change a purchase order once it is released under an authorization group, and when is it locked?
cards.body:
A **released** order under an authorization group can be changed only by users assigned to that group.
On loading, its status and group are read-only and its lines cannot be edited.
Once **Authorized**, the order cannot be saved again by anyone.
source_refs: Authorized or in-use records are locked [4:478dbad0-cd96-4aa4-bac7-6d61036ab7b0:77939] (rule:authorized-document-lock)

cards.title: Under multi-level approval, why can no user set a purchase order straight to Authorized?
cards.body:
Under **multi-level approval**, an order is authorized only through the approval entries, never by setting the status.
When the order is released, approval entries are created and **level 1** becomes ready to approve.
Setting Authorized directly, or before the **last level** approves, is refused.

cards.title: What must each approver record on a purchase order approval, and what extra is needed to reject?
cards.body:
Each approver records an **action**, Approve or Reject, on the selected approval entry.
A **rejection** must carry a comment, and under multi-level approval an authorization group must be chosen.
An entry already approved at that level cannot be approved again.

cards.title: Why is a user refused when they try to authorize a purchase order above their own amount limit?
cards.body:
A user can authorize an order only if its **net amount** falls inside one of their **limit ranges**.
Each user has From and To amounts set in configuration.
A larger order must be authorized by a user whose range covers it.

cards.title: Why can an approver not authorize a purchase order that is already completed or cancelled?
cards.body:
A **completed** or **cancelled** order cannot be authorized.
The order is already closed, so authorization is refused.
The refusal states whether the order is completed or cancelled.

cards.title: Why can the buyer not edit an authorized purchase order directly, and how is it changed instead?
cards.body:
An **authorized** order is locked; the buyer changes it through a **purchase order amendment**.
Each amendment is a versioned copy with its own number, reason and status, approved before it takes effect.
The live order always reflects the last authorized amendment.
source_refs: Authorized or in-use records are locked [4:478dbad0-cd96-4aa4-bac7-6d61036ab7b0:77939] (rule:authorized-document-lock)

cards.title: Why can the buyer not change the quantity of a completed, cancelled or short-closed line in an amendment?
cards.body:
On an amendment, a line whose status is **Completed**, **Cancel** or **Short Close** keeps its quantity.
Those lines are already closed, so their quantity is locked.
The buyer can still amend the quantity of lines that remain open.
source_refs: Authorized or in-use records are locked [4:478dbad0-cd96-4aa4-bac7-6d61036ab7b0:77939] (rule:authorized-document-lock)

cards.title: When must the buyer pick a reference document on a purchase order, and how is its date checked?
cards.body:
A **reference document** is required unless the reference type is Sales Order, Direct or Purchase Request.
The **order date** cannot be earlier than that reference's date.
When indents are required by settings, at least one source line must also be selected.
source_refs: Mandatory fields and valid selections on documents [4:478dbad0-cd96-4aa4-bac7-6d61036ab7b0:79742] (rule:mandatory-document-fields)

cards.title: What extra details must the buyer enter on a Direct purchase order that has no source document?
cards.body:
A **Direct** order needs a **department**, and is the only reference type that uses it.
When the company uses cost centers, each line of a Direct order also needs a **cost center**.
Until both are given, the save stops and names the missing department or the line without a cost center.

cards.title: How is the order rate worked out when the buyer converts the indent unit into a different order unit?
cards.body:
The **order rate** = indent rate x **first factor** / **second factor**.
The buyer enters both factors and the order unit; confirming them clears the order quantity for re-entry.
- Indent rate 20 per kg, first factor 25, second factor 1.
- Order rate = 20 x 25 / 1 = 500 per order unit.

cards.title: Which dates does the system check on each indent line the buyer selects for a purchase order?
cards.body:
Each selected **indent line** must pass three date checks before the order saves.
- The **order date** cannot be earlier than the indent date.
- A **schedule date** is required.
- The schedule date cannot be earlier than the order date.

cards.title: When an indent has reserved quantity, how must the buyer split the order quantity across reservations?
cards.body:
Where **reservation** exists, the selected reserve quantities must add up to the **order quantity**.
At least one reserve entry must be selected, and each one cannot exceed its **balance**.
For example, an order of 300 can take 200 and 100 from two reservations.

cards.title: Why can the buyer not add a transportation route or expense heads to an order with discrete items?
cards.body:
An order with **discrete items** cannot carry a **transportation route** or **expense heads**.
The save is refused until the route or expense heads are removed.
Inventory indents and discrete raw material indents also cannot be combined on one order.

cards.title: Why are intermediate, finished goods and phantom items refused on most purchase orders?
cards.body:
**Intermediate**, finished goods and phantom items are blocked on an order unless it is a **drop-shipment**.
A company rule configured for these item types also lifts the block.
Otherwise the buyer removes the item or changes the purchase type to drop-shipment.

cards.title: In what order does the system check a purchase order on save, and why does only one problem show at a time?
cards.body:
The system checks the order part by part and stops at the **first failure**, so one problem shows per save.
- Number, header, indents, shipping, accounts and terms come first.
- Then items, tax, GST, route, expenses and limits.
- Finally account assignment, company rules, **authorization group** and advances.

cards.title: An order of 480,000 under a group for up to 500,000 is raised to 530,000: what happens to its approvals?
cards.body:
The order moves to the group covering 530,000, and its earlier approval entries are cleared.
The **authorization group** follows the **net amount**, so a bigger order needs the approvers for that amount.
- The buyer raises the order at 480,000; group A covers up to 500,000.
- An approver at level 1 approves it.
- The buyer raises the amount to 530,000; the group is chosen again as group B.
- Because the group changed, the **approval entries** are cleared and start again.
Agree the final amount before release to avoid a second approval round.
source_refs: Purchase Order: Group by Net Amount [4:478dbad0-cd96-4aa4-bac7-6d61036ab7b0:80422] (rule:purchase-order-group-by-net-amount)

cards.title: Is a 1,200-unit line split as 500, 400 and 250 across three consignees allowed, and what fixes it?
cards.body:
No: 500 + 400 + 250 = 1,150, which is short of the line's 1,200, so the save is refused.
The buyer splits each line across **consignee** locations, and the parts must add up to the line quantity.
- Line quantity is 1,200.
- Consignee A 500, B 400, C 250 make 1,150.
- The system refuses: **consignee quantity** must equal 1,200.
- Changing C to 300 makes 1,200, and the line saves.
No consignee row may be zero or empty either.

cards.title: A purchase order is refused when someone tries to authorize it: what should they check, and in what order?
cards.body:
Check approvals, your own limit and the order's state, in that order.
Whoever is authorizing checks each point in turn.
- Under **multi-level approval**, has the last level approved through the approval entries?
- Does the **net amount** fall inside your own limit range?
- Is the order already **completed** or cancelled?
- Is it released under a group you are not assigned to?
If another user changed the order meanwhile, reload it and try again.
source_refs: Header and details are saved in one transaction [4:478dbad0-cd96-4aa4-bac7-6d61036ab7b0:77918] (rule:atomic-save)

cards.title: With an advance balance of 50,000 on a recurring agreement, can the buyer adjust 60,000 on a 40,000 order?
cards.body:
No: an adjustment cannot exceed the advance **balance amount** of 50,000.
On orders under a **recurring agreement**, open advances are adjusted against the order when the company's advance rule is active.
- Advance balance 50,000; order net amount 40,000.
- Adjusting 60,000 is refused: it exceeds the 50,000 balance.
- Adjusting 45,000 is within balance but above the net amount, so it warns.
- Leaving the advance unadjusted warns or blocks, per the **advance rule**.
Adjust 40,000 to match the order's net amount.

cards.title: What happens to the live purchase order when the buyer saves and then authorizes an amendment?
cards.body:
The live order changes only when the **amendment** is authorized; saving alone changes only the amendment copy.
Changes must be approved before they take effect, so the live order keeps the last authorized version.
- The buyer saves an amendment raising the rate from 200 to 210.
- Only the **amendment copy** is written; the live order still shows 200.
- On update, indent quantities are reversed and all lines rewritten.
- Once the amendment is **authorized**, the live order shows 210.
If the change must not apply, leave the amendment unauthorized.

cards.title: Why is a two-item order with inclusive freight refused once the buyer turns on PO rate validation?
cards.body:
Under **PO rate validation**, an order may hold one item, no route, and no **inclusive tax or charges**.
These limits apply when the company has configured the rule and the buyer marks the order for it.
- The buyer marks PO rate validation on an order with two items.
- The save is refused: only **one item** is allowed.
- Inclusive freight would also be refused, and so would any transportation route.
Split the items into separate orders and make the charges exclusive.
source_refs: Purchase Order: PO Rate Validation Rule [4:478dbad0-cd96-4aa4-bac7-6d61036ab7b0:80436] (rule:purchase-order-po-rate-validation-rule)

cards.title: Is a minus tolerance of 100% or of 200 units allowed on a 200-unit purchase order line?
cards.body:
No to both: **minus tolerance** must stay below 100% and below the line quantity.
**Tolerance** on a line is set either on a percentage basis or on a quantity basis.
- Line quantity is 200.
- Percentage basis: 100% is refused; 5% is allowed.
- Quantity basis: 200 is refused, since it equals the quantity; 10 is allowed.
Under a company rule, a line with no tolerance at all warns or blocks.
source_refs: Mandatory fields and valid selections on documents [4:478dbad0-cd96-4aa4-bac7-6d61036ab7b0:79742] (rule:mandatory-document-fields)

cards.title: A vendor in one state bills to a company location in another: which GST applies, and what is refused?
cards.body:
**IGST** applies across states; **SGST and CGST** are refused for an inter-state purchase.
The tax is checked by comparing the vendor location with the billed-to location in the same country.
- Vendor location in state A; billed-to location in state B.
- The buyer adds SGST and CGST: the save is refused.
- The buyer replaces them with IGST: the order saves.
- With both in state A, IGST is refused and SGST and CGST apply.
Under a company rule, an order with no GST at all warns before saving.
